verses.37:31: Then taking Joseph's tunic, they slaughtered a young goat and stained the tunic with blood.
verses.37:32: And they sent the multicolored tunic and brought it to their father, and said, "We found this; identify whether it is your son's tunic or not."
verses.37:33: And he recognized it and said, "It is my son's tunic! A vicious wild beast has devoured him; a wild beast has snatched Joseph away."
verses.37:34: Then Jacob tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his waist, and he mourned for his son for several days.
verses.37:35: And all his sons and daughters gathered together and came to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted, saying, "I will go down to my son mourning to Hades." And his father wept for him.
verses.37:36: Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph into Egypt to Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief cook.
verses.38:1: Now it came about at that time that Judah went down from his brothers and came as far as a certain Adullamite man whose name was Hirah.
verses.38:2: And there Judah saw a Canaanite man's daughter whose name was Shua; and he took her and went in to her.
verses.38:3: And she conceived and gave birth to a son, and called his name Er.
verses.38:4: And she conceived again and gave birth to a son, and called his name Onan.
verses.38:5: And once more she gave birth to a son, and called his name Shelah; and she was in Chezib when she gave birth to them.
verses.38:6: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar.
verses.38:7: Now Er, the firstborn of Judah, was wicked before the Lord, and God killed him.
verses.38:8: Then Judah said to Onan, "Go in to your brother's wife and marry her as brother-in-law, and raise up seed for your brother."
verses.38:9: And Onan, knowing that the seed would not be his, it happened that whenever he went in to his brother's wife, he poured it out on the ground so as not to give seed to his brother.
verses.38:10: And the thing appeared wicked before God that he did this, and He put this one to death also.
verses.38:11: Then Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, "Remain a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah grows up"; for he said, "Perhaps this one also will die like his brothers." So Tamar went away and remained in her father's house.
verses.38:12: Now the days multiplied, and Shua, Judah's wife, died; and when Judah was comforted, he went up to those who were shearing his sheep, he and Hirah his shepherd, the Adullamite, to Timnah.
verses.38:13: And it was reported to Tamar his daughter-in-law, saying, "Look, your father-in-law has gone up to Timnah to shear his sheep."
verses.38:14: And taking off her widowhood clothes from herself, she wrapped herself in a veil and adorned herself, and she sat by the gates of Enaim, which is on the way to Timnah; for she saw that his son Shelah had grown up, yet he had not given her to him as a wife.
verses.38:15: And when Judah saw her, he supposed her to be a prostitute, for she had covered her face, and he did not recognize her.
verses.38:16: And he turned aside from the road to her and said to her, "Let me come in to you"; for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, "What will you give me if you come in to me?"
verses.38:17: And he said, "I will send you a young goat from the flock." And she said, "If you give a pledge until you send it."
verses.38:18: And he said, "What pledge shall I give you?" And she said, "Your signet ring and the necklace and the staff that is in your hand." And he gave them to her, and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
verses.38:19: And getting up, she went away, and took off the veil from herself, and put on her widowhood clothes.
verses.38:20: Then Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his shepherd, the Adullamite, to recover the pledge from the woman; but he did not find her.
verses.38:21: And he asked the men who were in that place, "Where is the prostitute who was in Enaim by the road?" And they said, "There was no prostitute here."
verses.38:22: And he returned to Judah and said, "I did not find her, and the men from the place say that there is no prostitute here."
verses.38:23: And Judah said, "Let her keep them, so that we may not be ridiculed; I indeed have sent this young goat, but you have not found her."
verses.38:24: And it came about after three months that it was reported to Judah, saying, "Tamar your daughter-in-law has acted as a prostitute, and look, she is pregnant from prostitution." And Judah said, "Bring her out and let her be burned."
verses.38:25: But as she was being led out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, "I am pregnant by the man to whom these belong." And she said, "Identify whose are the signet ring and the necklace and this staff."
verses.38:26: And Judah recognized them and said, "Tamar has been justified more than I, because I did not give her to my son Shelah." And he did not know her again.
verses.38:27: And it came about, when she gave birth, that she had twins in her womb.
verses.38:28: And it came about, while she was giving birth, that one put out his hand first; and the midwife took a scarlet thread and tied it on his hand, saying, "This one will come out first."
verses.38:29: But as he drew back his hand, immediately his brother came out. And she said, "Why was a barrier broken through because of you?" And she called his name Perez.
verses.38:30: And after this his brother came out, on whose hand was the scarlet thread; and she called his name Zerah.
verses.39:1: Now Joseph was brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief cook, an Egyptian man, acquired him from the hands of the Ishmaelites who brought him down there.
verses.39:2: And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a successful man; and he was in the house with the Egyptian master.
verses.39:3: Now his master knew that the Lord was with him, and that whatever he did, the Lord prospered in his hands.
verses.39:4: And Joseph found favor before his master, and he was pleasing to him; and he appointed him over his house, and everything that belonged to him he gave into Joseph's hand.
verses.39:5: Now it came about after he was appointed over his house and over everything that belonged to him, that the Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph; and the blessing of the Lord came upon all his possessions, in the house and in the field.
verses.39:6: And he turned over everything that belonged to him into the hands of Joseph, and he knew nothing of his own affairs except the bread that he himself ate. And Joseph was handsome in form and very attractive in appearance.
verses.39:7: And it came about after these things that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph, and she said, "Lie with me."
verses.39:8: But he was not willing, and he said to his master's wife, "If my master knows nothing in his house because of me, and everything that belongs to him he has given into my hands,
verses.39:9: and he does not surpass me in anything in his house, nor has he withheld anything from me except you, because you are his wife, then how shall I do this wicked thing and sin before God?"
verses.39:10: And when she spoke to Joseph day after day, he did not listen to her to sleep with her, to be with her.
verses.39:11: Now a certain such day came about: Joseph went into the house to do his work, and no one was inside the house.
verses.39:12: And she pulled him by his garments, saying, "Lie with me." And leaving his garments, he fled and went outside.
verses.39:13: And it came about when she saw that he had left his garments in her hands and had fled and gone outside,
verses.39:14: that she called those who were in the house and spoke to them, saying, "Look, he brought in to us a Hebrew servant to mock us! He came in to me, saying, 'Lie with me,' and I cried out with a loud voice.
verses.39:15: And when he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, leaving his garments beside me, he fled and went outside."
verses.39:16: And she left the garments beside her until the master came into his house.
verses.39:17: And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, "The Hebrew servant whom you brought in to us came in to me to mock me, and he said to me, 'Lie with me.'
verses.39:18: And when he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garments beside me and fled and went outside."
verses.39:19: Now it came about when the master heard the words of his wife, all that she spoke to him, saying, "This is what your servant did to me," that he became furious with anger.
verses.39:20: And the master took Joseph and threw him into the stronghold, into the place where the king's prisoners are held there in the stronghold.
verses.39:21: And the Lord was with Joseph and poured down mercy upon him, and He gave him favor before the chief jailer.
verses.39:22: And the chief jailer gave the prison into Joseph's hand, and all those led away who were in the prison, and everything that they do there.
verses.39:23: The chief jailer knew nothing because of him, for everything was in Joseph's hand, because the Lord was with him; and whatever he himself did, the Lord prospered in his hands.
verses.40:1: Now it came about after these things that the chief cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the chief baker sinned against their lord, the king of Egypt.
verses.40:2: And Pharaoh was angry with his two eunuchs, with the chief cupbearer and with the chief baker;
verses.40:3: and he put them in custody with the chief jailer, into the prison, into the place where Joseph had been led away.
verses.40:4: And the chief warden entrusted them to Joseph, and he attended to them; and they were in custody for some days.
verses.40:5: And both of them saw a dream, each one a dream in one night, a vision of his dream--the chief cupbearer and the chief baker who belonged to the king of Egypt, who were in the prison.
verses.40:6: Now Joseph came in to them in the morning, and he saw them, and they were troubled.
verses.40:7: And he asked the eunuchs of Pharaoh who were with him in custody with his master, saying, "Why is it that your faces are gloomy today?"
verses.40:8: And they said to him, "We have seen a dream, and there is no one to interpret it." And Joseph said to them, "Is not their explanation through God? Tell me, then."
verses.40:9: And the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph and said, "In my sleep there was a vine before me,
verses.40:10: and on the vine were three stems; and it was flourishing, having brought forth shoots; the clusters of grapes were ripe.
verses.40:11: And the cup of Pharaoh was in my hand; and I took the grapes and squeezed them into the cup, and I gave the cup into the hands of Pharaoh."
verses.40:12: And Joseph said to him, "This is its interpretation: the three stems are three days.
verses.40:13: Three days more, and Pharaoh will remember your office and restore you to your office of chief cupbearer, and you will give the cup of Pharaoh into his hand according to your former office, as when you were serving as cupbearer.
verses.40:14: But remember me by yourself when it goes well for you, and show mercy toward me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this stronghold.
verses.40:15: For by theft I was stolen from the land of the Hebrews; and here I have done nothing, yet they threw me into this pit."
verses.40:16: And the chief baker saw that he had interpreted rightly, and he said to Joseph, "I too saw a dream, and I thought I was carrying three baskets of coarse-wheat loaves on my head;
verses.40:17: and in the top basket were some of all the foods that King Pharaoh eats, the work of a baker; and the birds of the sky were eating them from the basket on top of my head."
verses.40:18: And Joseph answered and said to him, "This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
verses.40:19: Within three days more, Pharaoh will remove your head from you and hang you on a tree, and the birds of the sky will eat your flesh from you."
verses.40:20: Now it came about on the third day--it was Pharaoh's birthday--that he made a banquet for all his servants; and he remembered the office of the chief cupbearer and the office of the chief baker in the midst of his servants.
verses.40:21: And he restored the chief cupbearer to his office, and he gave the cup into the hand of Pharaoh;
verses.40:22: but the chief baker he hanged, just as Joseph had interpreted to them.
verses.40:23: Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.
verses.41:1: Now it happened after two years of days that Pharaoh saw a dream. He thought he was standing by the river,
verses.41:2: and look, as if out of the river seven cows were coming up, fine in appearance and choice in flesh, and they were grazing in the reed-grass.
verses.41:3: And seven other cows were coming up after them out of the river, ugly in appearance and thin in flesh, and the cows were feeding beside the bank of the river in the reed-grass.
verses.41:4: And the seven cows that were ugly and thin in flesh devoured the seven cows that were fine in appearance and choice. Then Pharaoh woke up.
verses.41:5: And he dreamed a second time, and look, seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, choice and fine.
verses.41:6: And seven other ears of grain, thin and wind-blasted, were sprouting up after them.
verses.41:7: And the seven thin and wind-blasted ears of grain swallowed up the seven choice and full ears of grain. Then Pharaoh woke up, and it was a dream.
verses.41:8: Now morning came, and his soul was troubled, and he sent and called all the interpreters of Egypt and all its wise men; and Pharaoh recounted the dream to them, and there was no one to declare it to Pharaoh.
verses.41:9: And the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, "I recall my sin today.
verses.41:10: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and he put us in custody in the house of the chief jailer, both me and the chief baker.
verses.41:11: And we saw a dream in one night, I and he; each of us saw according to his own dream.
verses.41:12: Now there was there with us a young man, a Hebrew servant of the chief cook, and we told him, and he interpreted for us.
verses.41:13: And it came about just as he interpreted for us, so it also happened: I was restored to my office, and the other man was hanged."
verses.41:14: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and he brought him out of the stronghold; and they shaved him and changed his garment, and he came to Pharaoh.
verses.41:15: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I have seen a dream, and there is no one to interpret it; and I have heard people saying about you that when you hear dreams, you interpret them."
verses.41:16: And Joseph answered Pharaoh and said, "Apart from God, the welfare of Pharaoh will not be answered."
verses.41:17: Then Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, "In my sleep I thought I was standing on the bank of the river,
verses.41:18: and as if out of the river seven cows were coming up, fine in appearance and choice in flesh, and they were feeding in the reed-grass.
verses.41:19: And look, seven other cows were coming up behind them out of the river, bad and ugly in appearance and thin in flesh, and they were feeding in the reed-grass; such as these I never saw any uglier in all Egypt.
verses.41:20: And the seven ugly and thin cows devoured the first seven fine and choice cows,
verses.41:21: and they entered into their bellies, yet it was not apparent that they had entered into their bellies, and their appearance was ugly just as at the beginning. Then I woke up and fell asleep.
verses.41:22: And I saw again in my sleep, and as it were, seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, full and fine.
verses.41:23: And seven other ears of grain, thin and wind-blasted, were sprouting up next to them.
verses.41:24: And the seven thin and wind-blasted ears of grain swallowed up the seven fine and full ears of grain. So I told the interpreters, and there was no one to declare it to me."
verses.41:25: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, "The dream of Pharaoh is one; all that God is doing He has shown to Pharaoh.
verses.41:26: The seven fine cows are seven years, and the seven fine ears of grain are seven years; the dream of Pharaoh is one.
verses.41:27: And the seven thin cows coming up behind them are seven years, and the seven thin and wind-blasted ears of grain; they will be seven years of famine.
verses.41:28: Now the word that I have spoken to Pharaoh: all that God is doing He has shown to Pharaoh.
verses.41:29: Look, seven years are coming, great abundance in all the land of Egypt;
verses.41:30: and seven years of famine will come after them, and they will forget the plenty in all the land of Egypt, and the famine will consume the land.
verses.41:31: And the abundance will not be known upon the land because of the famine that will come after these things, for it will be exceedingly severe.
verses.41:32: And concerning the repeating of the dream to Pharaoh twice, it is because the word from God will be true, and God will hasten to do it.
verses.41:33: Now therefore look out for a prudent and discerning man, and appoint him over the land of Egypt;
verses.41:34: and let Pharaoh act and appoint district governors over the land, and let them take a fifth of all the produce of the land of Egypt during the seven years of abundance,
verses.41:35: and let them gather all the food of these seven fine years that are coming; and let the grain be gathered under the hand of Pharaoh, let food be gathered in the cities.
verses.41:36: And the food will be kept for the land for the seven years of the famine that will be in the land of Egypt, and the land will not be wiped out in the famine."
verses.41:37: Now the words were pleasing before Pharaoh and before all his servants.
verses.41:38: And Pharaoh said to all his servants, "Can we find a man like this, who has the spirit of God in him?"
verses.41:39: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Since God has shown you all these things, there is no man more prudent and more discerning than you.
verses.41:40: You will be over my house, and at your mouth all my people will obey; only in the throne will I surpass you."
verses.41:41: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "See, I appoint you today over all the land of Egypt."
verses.41:42: And Pharaoh took off the ring from his hand and put it on Joseph's hand, and he clothed him in a fine linen garment, and he placed a gold collar around his neck.
verses.41:43: And he had him mount the second of his chariots, and a herald proclaimed before him; and he appointed him over the whole land of Egypt.
verses.41:44: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh; without you no one will lift up his hand in all the land of Egypt."
verses.41:45: And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Psonthomphanech; and he gave to him Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, as a wife.
verses.41:46: Now Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh and passed through all the land of Egypt.
verses.41:47: And during the seven years of abundance the land produced sheaves;
verses.41:48: and he gathered all the food of the seven years in which the abundance was in the land of Egypt, and he placed the food in the cities; the food of the fields of the city around it, On, he placed in it.
verses.41:49: And Joseph gathered grain like the sand of the sea, exceedingly much, until he was unable to count it, for there was no number.
verses.41:50: Now to Joseph two sons were born before the seven years of the famine came, whom Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of Heliopolis, bore to him.
verses.41:51: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, saying, "Because God has made me forget all my toils and all the things of my father."
verses.41:52: And the name of the second he called Ephraim, "Because God has exalted me in the land of my humiliation."
verses.41:53: Then the seven years of abundance that occurred in the land of Egypt passed away,
verses.41:54: and the seven years of the famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. And there was famine in all the earth, and in all the land of Egypt there was no bread.
verses.41:55: And all the land of Egypt grew hungry, and all the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread; and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, "Go to Joseph, and whatever he says to you, do it."
verses.41:56: And the famine was over the face of all the earth; and Joseph opened all the granaries and was selling to all the Egyptians.
verses.41:57: And all the countries came to Egypt to buy from Joseph, for the famine prevailed in all the earth.
verses.42:1: Now when Jacob saw that there was a sale in Egypt, he said to his sons, "Why are you being idle?
verses.42:2: Look, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt; go down there and buy a little food for us, so that we may live and not die."
verses.42:3: So the ten brothers of Joseph went down to buy grain from Egypt.
verses.42:4: But Benjamin, the brother of Joseph, he did not send with his brothers, for he said, "Perhaps an illness might happen to him."
verses.42:5: So the sons of Israel came to buy with those who were coming, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
verses.42:6: Now Joseph was ruler of the land; he was the one who sold to all the people of the land. And when the brothers of Joseph came, they bowed down to him face down to the ground.
verses.42:7: And when Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, yet he acted like a stranger toward them and spoke harsh things to them, and he said to them, "Where have you come from?" And they said, "From the land of Canaan, to buy food."
verses.42:8: Now Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.
verses.42:9: And Joseph remembered the dreams that he himself had seen. And he said to them, "You are spies; you have come to observe the tracks of the country."
verses.42:10: And they said, "No, lord; we, your servants, have come to buy food.
verses.42:11: We are all sons of one man; we are peaceable; your servants are not spies."
verses.42:12: But he said to them, "No, rather you have come to see the tracks of the land."
verses.42:13: And they said, "We, your servants, are twelve brothers in the land of Canaan; and look, the youngest is with our father today, and the other one is no more."
verses.42:14: And Joseph said to them, "This is what I have spoken to you, saying that you are spies:
verses.42:15: by this you will be revealed: by the health of Pharaoh, you will certainly not go out from here unless your youngest brother comes here.
verses.42:16: Send one from among you, and fetch your brother, but as for you, be led away until your words become evident, whether you are telling the truth or not; otherwise, by the health of Pharaoh, surely you are spies."
verses.42:17: And he put them in prison for three days.
verses.42:18: Then on the third day he said to them, "Do this, and you will live, for I fear God:
verses.42:19: if you are peaceable, let one of your brothers be held in prison, but you yourselves go and carry away the purchase of your grain supply,
verses.42:20: and bring your youngest brother down to me, and your words will be believed; otherwise, you will die." And they did so.
verses.42:21: And each one said to his brother, "Yes, for we are in sin concerning our brother, because we disregarded the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen to him; on account of this, this distress has come upon us."
verses.42:22: And Reuben answered and said to them, "Did I not speak to you, saying, 'Do not wrong the boy'? Yet you did not listen to me; and look, his blood is being demanded."
verses.42:23: Now they did not know that Joseph understood, for the interpreter was between them.
verses.42:24: And turning away from them, Joseph wept. And again he approached them and spoke to them; and he took Simeon from them and bound him before them.
verses.42:25: Then Joseph commanded to fill their vessels with grain, and to return each one's silver into his sack, and to give them provisions for the journey. And so it was done for them.
verses.42:26: And having loaded the grain onto their donkeys, they departed from there.
verses.42:27: Now when one untied his bag to give fodder to his donkeys where they lodged, he saw his bundle of silver, and it was on top of the mouth of the bag.
verses.42:28: And he said to his brothers, "My silver has been returned to me, and look, here it is in my bag." And their heart was astonished, and they were troubled, saying to one another, "What is this that God has done to us?"
verses.42:29: And they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan, and reported to him all the things that had happened to them, saying,
verses.42:30: "The man, the lord of the land, spoke harsh things to us, and put us in prison as spying out the land.
verses.42:31: And we said to him, 'We are peaceable; we are not spies;
verses.42:32: we are twelve brothers, sons of our father; the one is no more, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan.'
verses.42:33: And the man, the lord of the land, said to us, 'By this we will know that you are peaceable: leave one brother here with me, and taking the purchase of your grain supply, depart;
verses.42:34: and bring your youngest brother to me, and I will know that you are not spies, but that you are peaceable; and I will return your brother to you, and you may trade in the land.'"
verses.42:35: And it happened as they were emptying their sacks that each one's bundle of silver was in their sack; and they and their father saw their bundles of silver, and they were afraid.
verses.42:36: And Jacob their father said to them, "You have made me childless: Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you will take Benjamin! All these things have come upon me."
verses.42:37: And Reuben spoke to his father, saying, "Kill my two sons if I do not bring him to you; give him into my hand, and I will bring him back to you."
verses.42:38: But he said, "My son will not go down with you, for his brother died, and he alone has been left; and it will happen that he falls ill on the road that you go, and you will bring down my old age with grief to Hades."
verses.43:1: Now the famine grew severe upon the land.
verses.43:2: And it happened when they had finished eating up the grain that they had brought from Egypt, that their father said to them, "Go again and buy a little food for us."
verses.43:3: And Judah spoke to him, saying, "The man solemnly warned us, saying, 'You will not see my face unless your youngest brother comes down to me.'
verses.43:4: So if you send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you;
verses.43:5: but if you do not send our brother with us, we will not go, for the man spoke to us, saying, 'You will not see my face unless your youngest brother is with you.'"
verses.43:6: And Israel said, "Why did you treat me badly, by reporting to the man whether you had a brother?"
verses.43:7: And they said, "The man closely questioned us and about our family, saying, 'Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother?' And we reported to him according to his questioning. Could we have known whether he would say to us, 'Bring your brother'?"
verses.43:8: And Judah said to Israel his father, "Send the boy with me, and we will arise and go, so that we may live and not die, both we and you and our dependents.
verses.43:9: I myself take responsibility for him; require him from my hand. If I do not bring him to you and set him before you, I will have sinned against you all the days.
verses.43:10: For if we had not delayed, we would already have returned twice."
verses.43:11: Then Israel their father said to them, "If it is so, do this: take some of the fruits of the land in your vessels, and bring down gifts to the man—some resin and honey, incense and myrrh oil and terebinth and walnuts.
verses.43:12: And take double the silver in your hands; return with you the silver that was returned in your bags; perhaps it is an oversight.
verses.43:13: And take your brother, and arise and go down to the man.
verses.43:14: And may my God grant you favor before the man, and send back your one brother and Benjamin; for as for me, just as I have been made childless, I am made childless."
verses.43:15: So the men took these gifts, and they took double the silver in their hands, and Benjamin; and rising up, they went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph.
verses.43:16: And Joseph saw them and Benjamin, his brother by the same mother, and he commanded the one over his house to bring the men into the house: "And slaughter animals and prepare them, for the men will eat bread with me at midday."
verses.43:17: And the man did just as Joseph had said, and brought the men into the house of Joseph.
verses.43:18: And when the men saw that they had been brought into the house of Joseph, they said, "Because of the silver that was returned in our bags the first time, we are being brought in, to accuse us falsely and to attack us, to take us as servants, and our donkeys."
verses.43:19: So approaching the man who was over the house of Joseph, they spoke to him at the gateway of the house,
verses.43:20: saying, "We beg you, lord: we came down the first time to buy food;
verses.43:21: and it happened when we came to the lodging place and opened our bags, here was each one's silver in his bag. Our silver by weight we have now returned in our bags,
verses.43:22: and we have brought other silver with us to buy food; we do not know who put the silver into our bags."
verses.43:23: And the man said to them, "Be at ease; do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your fathers has given you treasures in your bags; and I have received your approved silver in full." And he brought Simeon out to them.
verses.43:24: And he brought water to wash their feet, and he brought fodder for their donkeys.
verses.43:25: And they prepared the gifts until Joseph came at midday, for they had heard that he was going to dine there.
verses.43:26: Now Joseph entered the house, and they brought to him into the house the gifts that they had in their hands, and they bowed down to him face down to the ground.
verses.43:27: And he asked them, "How are you?" And he said to them, "Is your aged father of whom you spoke in good health? Is he still alive?"
verses.43:28: And they said, "Your servant our father is in good health; he is still alive." And he said, "Blessed is that man by God." And bending low, they bowed down.
verses.43:29: And lifting up his eyes, Joseph saw Benjamin, his brother by the same mother, and said to them, "Is this your youngest brother, whom you spoke of bringing to me?" And he said, "May God have mercy on you, child."
verses.43:30: And Joseph was troubled, for his inward parts were churning over his brother, and he sought to weep; so entering the inner room, he wept there.
verses.43:31: And having washed his face, he came out and restrained himself, and said, "Set out bread."
verses.43:32: And they set it before him by himself, and before them by themselves, and before the Egyptians who dined with him by themselves; for the Egyptians could not eat bread together with the Hebrews, for every shepherd of sheep is an abomination to the Egyptians.
verses.43:33: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth; and the men were astonished, each one toward his brother.
verses.43:34: And they carried a portion from him to them; and Benjamin's portion was enlarged five times beyond the portions of all in comparison with theirs. And they drank and became drunk with him.
verses.44:1: And Joseph commanded the one who was over his house, saying, "Fill the men's bags with as much food as they are able to carry, and put each one's silver at the mouth of his bag,
verses.44:2: and put my silver cup into the bag of the youngest, and the price of his grain." And it was done according to the word of Joseph, just as he spoke.
verses.44:3: The morning dawned, and the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
verses.44:4: And when they had gone out of the city, they had not gone far away, and Joseph spoke to the one over his house, saying, "Get up, pursue after the men, and you will overtake them and say to them, 'Why have you repaid me evil for good?
verses.44:5: Why did you steal my silver cup? Is this not the one from which my lord drinks? And he indeed practices divination with it. You have accomplished evil things in what you have done.'"
verses.44:6: And having found them, he spoke to them according to these words.
verses.44:7: And they said to him, "Why does my lord speak according to these words? Far be it from your servants to do this thing.
verses.44:8: If we returned to you from the land of Canaan the silver that we found in our bags, how could we steal silver or gold from the house of your lord?
verses.44:9: The one of your servants with whom the cup is found, let him die; and we also will be servants to our lord."
verses.44:10: And he said, "And now, as you say, so it will be: the man with whom the cup is found, he will be my servant, and you will be innocent."
verses.44:11: And they hurried and each one lowered his bag to the ground, and each one opened his bag.
verses.44:12: And he searched, beginning from the oldest until he came to the youngest, and he found the cup in Benjamin's bag.
verses.44:13: And they tore their garments, and each one placed his bag upon his donkey, and they returned to the city.
verses.44:14: And Judah and his brothers came in to Joseph, while he was still there, and they fell before him to the ground.
verses.44:15: And Joseph said to them, "What is this deed you have done? Do you not know that a man such as I will surely practice divination?"
verses.44:16: And Judah said, "What shall we answer my lord, or what shall we speak, or how shall we be justified? God has found the wrongdoing of your servants. Look, we are household servants to our lord, both we and the one with whom the cup was found."
verses.44:17: And Joseph said, "Far be it from me to do this thing. The man with whom the cup was found, he will be my servant; but as for you, go up in safety to your father."
verses.44:18: And Judah drew near to him and said, "I beg you, my lord, let your servant speak a word before you, and do not be angry with your servant, for you are after Pharaoh.
verses.44:19: My lord, you asked your servants, saying, 'Do you have a father or a brother?'
verses.44:20: And we said to my lord, 'We have an elderly father, and a younger child of his old age; and his brother died, and he alone was left to his father, and his father loved him.'
verses.44:21: And you said to your servants, 'Bring him down to me, and I will take care of him.'
verses.44:22: And we said to my lord, 'The child will not be able to leave his father; and if he leaves his father, he will die.'
verses.44:23: But you said to your servants, 'Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.'
verses.44:24: And it came about when we went up to your servant, our father, that we reported to him the words of my lord.
verses.44:25: And our father said to us, 'Go again, buy us a little food.'
verses.44:26: And we said, 'We will not be able to go down; rather, if our youngest brother goes down with us, we will go down, for we will not be able to see the face of the man while our youngest brother is not with us.'
verses.44:27: And your servant our father said to us, 'You know that my wife bore me two.
verses.44:28: And the one went out from me, and you said, "He has been devoured by a wild beast," and I have not seen him since.
verses.44:29: Therefore, if you take this one also from my presence and sickness befalls him on the way, then you will bring down my old age with grief to Hades.'
verses.44:30: Now therefore, if I go in to your servant, our father, and the boy is not with us, since his soul hangs upon this one's soul,
verses.44:31: then it will happen when he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die, and your servants will bring down the old age of your servant, our father, with sorrow to Hades.
verses.44:32: For your servant has become surety for the child from my father, saying, 'If I do not bring him to you and set him before you, I will have sinned against my father all the days.'
verses.44:33: Now therefore, I will remain with you as a servant instead of the child, a household servant of my lord; and let the child go up with the brothers.
verses.44:34: For how shall I go up to my father when the child is not with us? So that I may not see the evils that will find my father."
verses.45:1: And Joseph was not able to restrain himself before all those standing beside him, but he said, "Send everyone away from me." And no one stood beside Joseph any longer when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.
verses.45:2: And he let out a cry with weeping; and all the Egyptians heard, and it became heard in the house of Pharaoh.
verses.45:3: And Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt. Is my father still alive?" And the brothers were not able to answer him, for they were dismayed.
verses.45:4: And he said, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
verses.45:5: Now therefore, do not be grieved, nor let it seem hard to you that you sold me here, for God sent me before you for life.
verses.45:6: For this is the second year of famine upon the earth, and there are still five years remaining in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.
verses.45:7: For God sent me before you to leave behind a remnant of you on the earth, and to nourish a great survival of you.
verses.45:8: Now therefore, it was not you who sent me here, but God; and He made me as a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler of all the land of Egypt.
verses.45:9: Hurry therefore and go up to my father, and say to him, 'Thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all the land of Egypt; come down therefore to me and do not delay.
verses.45:10: And you will dwell in the land of Goshen of Arabia, and you will be near me, you and your sons and your sons' sons, your sheep and your cattle and all that belongs to you there.
verses.45:11: And I will nourish you there, for there are still five years of famine, so that you may not be wiped out, you and your sons and all your possessions.'
verses.45:12: Look, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that is speaking to you.
verses.45:13: Therefore report to my father all my glory in Egypt and all that you have seen, and hurry and bring my father down here."
verses.45:14: And falling upon the neck of Benjamin his brother, he fell upon him; and Benjamin wept upon his neck.
verses.45:15: And having kissed all his brothers, he wept over them; and after these things his brothers spoke to him.
verses.45:16: And the report was spread abroad into the house of Pharaoh, saying, "Joseph's brothers have come." And Pharaoh and his attendants rejoiced.
verses.45:17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Say to your brothers, 'Do this: load your carts and go away to the land of Canaan,
verses.45:18: and taking your father and your possessions, come to me; and I will give you of all the good things of Egypt, and you will eat the marrow of the land.'
verses.45:19: And you, command these things: for them to take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and your wives, and taking up your father, come.
verses.45:20: And do not spare your goods with your eyes, for all the good things of Egypt will be yours."
verses.45:21: And the sons of Israel did so. And Joseph gave them wagons according to the things spoken by Pharaoh the king, and he gave them provisions for the way.
verses.45:22: And to all he gave double robes, and to Benjamin he gave three hundred gold pieces and five changes of robes.
verses.45:23: And to his father he sent in the same manner, and ten donkeys carrying of all the good things of Egypt, and ten mules carrying bread for his father for the way.
verses.45:24: And he sent away his brothers, and they went; and he said to them, "Do not be angry on the way."
verses.45:25: And they went up out of Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father,
verses.45:26: and they reported to him, saying, "Your son Joseph is alive, and he rules over all the land of Egypt." And Jacob's mind was stunned, for he did not believe them.
verses.45:27: And they spoke to him all the things spoken by Joseph, all that he had said to them; and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to take him up, the spirit of Jacob their father revived.
verses.45:28: And Israel said, "It is a great thing to me if my son Joseph is still alive; I will go and see him before I die."
verses.46:1: Now Israel set out, he and all that was his, and they came to the Well of the Oath, and there he offered a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac.
verses.46:2: And God spoke to Israel in a vision of the night, saying, "Jacob, Jacob." And he said, "What is it?"
verses.46:3: And He said, "I am the God of your fathers. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there;
verses.46:4: and I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will bring you up in the end; and Joseph will lay his hands upon your eyes."
verses.46:5: Then Jacob rose up from the Well of the Oath, and the sons of Israel took up their father and the dependents and their wives onto the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him.
verses.46:6: And having taken their possessions and all the property that they had acquired from the land of Canaan, Jacob entered into Egypt, and all his seed with him,
verses.46:7: sons and the sons of his sons with him, daughters and daughters of his sons with him; and he brought all his seed into Egypt.
verses.46:8: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel who entered into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: the firstborn of Jacob was Reuben.
verses.46:9: And the sons of Reuben: Hanoch and Pallu, Hezron and Carmi.
verses.46:10: And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jachin and Zohar and Samuel, the son of the Canaanite woman.
verses.46:11: And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
verses.46:12: And the sons of Judah: Er and Onan and Shelah and Perez and Zerah. Now Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Perez were Hezron and Jemuel.
verses.46:13: And the sons of Issachar: Tola and Puvah and Jashub and Zambram.
verses.46:14: And the sons of Zebulun: Sered and Hezron and Jahleel.
verses.46:15: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, and Dinah his daughter; all the souls, sons and daughters, were thirty-three.
verses.46:16: And the sons of Gad: Ziphion and Haggi and Shuni and Thasoban and Eri and Arodi and Areli.
verses.46:17: And the sons of Asher: Imnah and Jessai and Jeul and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
verses.46:18: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob, sixteen souls.
verses.46:19: And the sons of Rachel, the wife of Jacob: Joseph and Benjamin.
verses.46:20: Now sons were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of Heliopolis, bore to him: Manasseh and Ephraim. And sons were born to Manasseh, whom the Syrian concubine bore to him: Machir; and Machir fathered Gilead. And the sons of Ephraim, the brother of Manasseh: Sutalaam and Taam. And the sons of Sutalaam: Edem.
verses.46:21: And the sons of Benjamin: Bela and Chobor and Ashbel. And the sons of Bela were Gera and Naaman and Ehi and Rosh and Muppim and Huppim; and Gera fathered Ard.
verses.46:22: These are the sons of Rachel whom Jacob fathered; all the souls were eighteen.
verses.46:23: And the sons of Dan: Hushim.
verses.46:24: And the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel and Guni and Jezer and Shillem.
verses.46:25: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter, and she bore these to Jacob; all the souls were seven.
verses.46:26: Now all the souls who entered with Jacob into Egypt, those who came out from his loins, apart from the wives of Jacob's sons, all the souls were sixty-six.
verses.46:27: And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in the land of Egypt were nine souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob who entered into Egypt were seventy-five.
verses.46:28: Now he sent Judah ahead of them to Joseph to meet him at Heroonpolis, into the land of Rameses.
verses.46:29: And Joseph hitched his chariots and went up to meet Israel his father at Heroonpolis; and when he appeared to him, he fell upon his neck and wept with abundant weeping.
verses.46:30: And Israel said to Joseph, "I may die from now on, since I have seen your face, for you are still alive."
verses.46:31: And Joseph said to his brothers, "I will go up and report to Pharaoh, and I will say to him, 'My brothers and the house of my father, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me;
verses.46:32: and the men are shepherds, for they were men who keep livestock; and they have brought their livestock and their cattle and all that is theirs.'
verses.46:33: So if Pharaoh calls you and says to you, 'What is your occupation?'
verses.46:34: you will say, 'We, your servants, are men who keep livestock from youth until now, both we and our fathers,' so that you may dwell in the land of Goshen of Arabia; for every shepherd of sheep is an abomination to the Egyptians."
verses.47:1: Then Joseph came and reported to Pharaoh, saying, "My father and brothers, and their livestock and cattle and all that is theirs, have come from the land of Canaan; and look, they are in the land of Goshen."
verses.47:2: And from among his brothers he took five men and set them before Pharaoh.
verses.47:3: And Pharaoh said to Joseph's brothers, "What is your occupation?" And they said to Pharaoh, "Your servants are shepherds of sheep, both we and our fathers."
verses.47:4: And they said to Pharaoh, "We have come to sojourn in the land, for there is no pasture for the livestock of your servants, because the famine has grown severe in the land of Canaan. Now therefore we will dwell in the land of Goshen." And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Let them dwell in the land of Goshen; and if you know that there are capable men among them, appoint them rulers over my livestock." Now Jacob and his sons came into Egypt to Joseph, and Pharaoh king of Egypt heard.
verses.47:5: And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, saying, "Your father and your brothers have come to you;
verses.47:6: look, the land of Egypt is before you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best land."
verses.47:7: Then Joseph brought in Jacob his father and set him before Pharaoh; and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
verses.47:8: And Pharaoh said to Jacob, "How many are the years of the days of your life?"
verses.47:9: And Jacob said to Pharaoh, "The days of the years of my life that I sojourn are one hundred thirty years. Short and evil have the days of the years of my life been; they have not reached the days of the years of the life of my fathers, the days that they sojourned."
verses.47:10: And having blessed Pharaoh, Jacob went out from him.
verses.47:11: And Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best land, in the land of Rameses, just as Pharaoh had commanded.
verses.47:12: And Joseph measured out grain to his father and to his brothers and to all the house of his father, according to each person.
verses.47:13: Now there was no grain in all the land, for the famine grew exceedingly severe; and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan failed because of the famine.
verses.47:14: And Joseph gathered all the silver that was found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan for the grain that they were buying, and he measured out grain to them; and Joseph brought all the silver into the house of Pharaoh.
verses.47:15: And all the silver failed from the land of Egypt and from the land of Canaan. Then all the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying, "Give us bread! And why should we die before you? For our silver has failed."
verses.47:16: And Joseph said to them, "Bring your livestock, and I will give you bread in exchange for your livestock, if your silver has failed."
verses.47:17: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses and for the sheep and for the cattle and for the donkeys; and he nourished them with bread in exchange for all their livestock in that year.
verses.47:18: And that year came to an end, and they came to him in the second year and said to him, "Let us not be wiped out from our lord; for if our silver and possessions and livestock have failed to you, the lord, then nothing is left to us before the lord except our own body and our land.
verses.47:19: So that we may not die before you and the land become desolate, acquire us and our land in exchange for bread, and we and our land will be servants of Pharaoh. Give seed so that we may sow and not die, and the land will become desolate."
verses.47:20: So Joseph acquired all the land of the Egyptians for Pharaoh, for the Egyptians sold their land to Pharaoh, because the famine prevailed over them; and the land became Pharaoh's,
verses.47:21: and he enslaved the people to him as servants, from one end of the borders of Egypt to the other,
verses.47:22: apart from the land of the priests alone; Joseph did not acquire this, for by a grant Pharaoh gave a gift to the priests, and they ate the grant that Pharaoh gave them; therefore they did not sell their land.
verses.47:23: Then Joseph said to all the Egyptians, "Look, I have acquired you and your land today for Pharaoh. Take seed for yourselves and sow the land;
verses.47:24: and when its produce comes, you will give the fifth part to Pharaoh; and the four parts will be for you yourselves, for seed for the land and for food for you and for all your households."
verses.47:25: And they said, "You have saved us! We have found favor before our lord, and we will be servants of Pharaoh."
verses.47:26: And Joseph established it for them as a statute until this day over the land of Egypt, to pay a fifth to Pharaoh, apart from the land of the priests alone; it did not belong to Pharaoh.
verses.47:27: Now Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and they gained an inheritance in it, and they multiplied exceedingly.
verses.47:28: And Jacob lived on in the land of Egypt seventeen years; and the days of Jacob, of the years of his life, were one hundred forty-seven years.
verses.47:29: Now the days of Israel drew near for him to die, and he called his son Joseph and said to him, "If I have found favor before you, place your hand under my thigh, and you will show mercy and truth toward me, not to bury me in Egypt;
verses.47:30: rather, I will sleep with my fathers, and you will carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their tomb." And he said, "I will do according to your word."
verses.47:31: And he said, "Swear to me." And he swore to him. And Israel bowed in worship upon the top of his staff.
verses.48:1: Now it happened after these things that it was reported to Joseph, "Your father is ill." And taking along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, he came to Jacob.
verses.48:2: And it was reported to Jacob, saying, "Look, your son Joseph is coming to you." And Israel strengthened himself and sat up on the bed.
verses.48:3: And Jacob said to Joseph, "My God appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me,
verses.48:4: and He said to me, 'Look, I will cause you to grow and multiply you, and I will make you into assemblies of nations, and I will give this land to you and to your seed after you for an everlasting possession.'
verses.48:5: Now therefore, your two sons who were born to you in Egypt before I came to Egypt to you are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh will be mine, just like Reuben and Simeon.
verses.48:6: But the children whom you may father after these will be under the name of their brothers; they will be called in their brothers' allotments.
verses.48:7: And as for me, when I was coming from Mesopotamia of Syria, Rachel your mother died in the land of Canaan, as I was approaching the racecourse of Chabratha of the land, to come to Ephrathah; and I buried her on the road of the racecourse; this is Bethlehem."
verses.48:8: And when Israel saw the sons of Joseph, he said, "Who are these to you?"
verses.48:9: And Joseph said to his father, "They are my sons, whom God has given me here." And Jacob said, "Bring them to me so that I may bless them."
verses.48:10: Now the eyes of Israel had grown dim from old age, and he was not able to see. And he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
verses.48:11: And Israel said to Joseph, "Look, I have not been deprived of your face, and look, God has shown me your seed as well."
verses.48:12: And Joseph brought them out from his knees, and they bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.
verses.48:13: And Joseph took his two sons, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel's left, and Manasseh on his left toward Israel's right, and brought them near to him.
verses.48:14: But Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it upon the head of Ephraim (now he was the younger), and his left hand upon the head of Manasseh, crossing his hands.
verses.48:15: And he blessed them and said, "The God whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac pleased in His sight, the Lord who has nourished me from youth until this day,
verses.48:16: the angel who delivers me from all evils, may He bless these boys; and my name will be called upon them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and may they be multiplied into a great multitude upon the earth."
verses.48:17: And when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, it appeared grievous to him; and Joseph took hold of his father's hand to lift it from the head of Ephraim onto the head of Manasseh.
verses.48:18: And Joseph said to his father, "Not so, father; for this one is the firstborn. Place your right hand upon his head."
verses.48:19: And he was not willing, but said, "I know, child, I know. He too will become a people, and he too will be exalted; yet his younger brother will be greater than he, and his seed will become a multitude of nations."
verses.48:20: And he blessed them on that day, saying, "In you Israel will be blessed, saying, 'May God make you like Ephraim and like Manasseh.'" And he placed Ephraim before Manasseh.
verses.48:21: And Israel said to Joseph, "Look, I am dying, and God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers.
verses.48:22: And as for me, I give you Shechem, singled out above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorites with my sword and bow."
verses.49:1: Now Jacob called his sons and said to them, "Gather together, so that I may declare to you what will happen to you in the last days.
verses.49:2: Gather together and listen to me, sons of Jacob; listen to Israel, listen to your father.
verses.49:3: Reuben, my firstborn, you are my strength and the beginning of my children; hard to bear and hard, self-willed.
verses.49:4: You acted insolently like water; do not boil over! For you went up onto your father's bed; then you defiled the couch where you went up.
verses.49:5: Simeon and Levi are brothers; they accomplished injustice by their own choice.
verses.49:6: Into their council may my soul not enter, and at their gathering may my liver not contend; because in their wrath they killed men, and in their passion they hamstrung a bull.
verses.49:7: Cursed is their wrath because it is self-willed, and their fury because it has been hardened; I will divide them in Jacob, and I will scatter them in Israel.
verses.49:8: Judah, may your brothers praise you; your hands will be on the back of your enemies; the sons of your father will bow down to you.
verses.49:9: Judah is a lion's cub; from a shoot, my son, you have gone up. Lying down, you slept like a lion and like a cub; who will rouse him?
verses.49:10: A ruler will not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until the things reserved for him come, and he is the expectation of nations.
verses.49:11: Tying his colt to a vine, and the colt of his donkey to the tendril, he will wash his robe in wine, and his cloak in the blood of the grape.
verses.49:12: His eyes are more gladdening than wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.
verses.49:13: Zebulun will dwell by the sea, and he himself beside a harbor of ships, and he will extend as far as Sidon.
verses.49:14: Issachar desired what is good, resting in the midst of the allotments;
verses.49:15: and seeing the resting place, that it was good, and the land, that it was rich, he put his shoulder under to labor and became a farming man.
verses.49:16: Dan will judge his own people, just like one tribe in Israel.
verses.49:17: And let Dan become a serpent on a road, lying in wait upon a path, biting a horse's heel, and the rider will fall backward,
verses.49:18: waiting for the salvation of the Lord.
verses.49:19: Gad, a raiding band will raid him, but he himself will raid them at their heels.
verses.49:20: Asher, rich is his bread, and he himself will provide delicacies for rulers.
verses.49:21: Naphtali is a spreading trunk, yielding beauty in its produce.
verses.49:22: Joseph is a grown son, my enviable grown son, my youngest son; return to me,
verses.49:23: against whom, plotting together, they hurled insults, and masters of arrows held a grudge against him.
verses.49:24: And their bows were shattered with might, and the sinews of the arms of their hand were loosened by the hand of the Mighty One of Jacob; from there is the one who strengthened Israel, from the God of your father.
verses.49:25: And my God helped you, and He blessed you with a blessing of heaven above, and a blessing of the earth that holds all things, on account of the blessing of breasts and womb,
verses.49:26: the blessing of your father and your mother; it has prevailed over the blessings of enduring mountains and over the blessings of everlasting hills. They will be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the brothers whom he led.
verses.49:27: Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he will still eat, and toward evening he gives food."
verses.49:28: All these are the twelve sons of Jacob, and these things their father spoke to them; and their father blessed them, each one according to his own blessing he blessed them.
verses.49:29: And he said to them, "I am being added to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,
verses.49:30: in the double cave that is opposite Mamre in the land of Canaan, the cave that Abraham acquired from Ephron the Hittite as a possession for a tomb.
verses.49:31: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; there they buried Leah,
verses.49:32: in the possession of the field and of the cave that is in it, from the sons of Heth."
verses.49:33: And Jacob finished instructing his sons, and lifting up his feet onto the bed, he expired and was added to his people.
verses.50:1: And Joseph fell upon his father's face and wept over him and kissed him.
verses.50:2: And Joseph commanded his servants the embalmers to embalm his father; and the embalmers embalmed Israel.
verses.50:3: And he completed forty days for them, for in this way the days of burial are numbered; and Egypt mourned for him seventy days.
verses.50:4: Now when the days of mourning had passed, Joseph spoke to the officials of Pharaoh, saying, "If I have found favor before you, speak concerning me in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,
verses.50:5: 'My father made me swear, saying, "In the tomb that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you will bury me." Now therefore, I will go up and bury my father, and I will return.'"
verses.50:6: And Pharaoh said, "Go up, bury your father, just as he made you swear."
verses.50:7: And Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh and the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
verses.50:8: and all the household of Joseph, and his brothers, and all his father's house, and his relatives; and they left behind the sheep and the cattle in the land of Goshen.
verses.50:9: And both chariots and horsemen went up with him, and the company was very great.
verses.50:10: And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and they lamented for him with a great and very strong lamentation; and they observed the mourning for his father seven days.
verses.50:11: And the inhabitants of the land of Canaan saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad and said, "This is a great mourning for the Egyptians." Therefore he called its name Mourning of Egypt, which is beyond the Jordan.
verses.50:12: And his sons did so for him, and they buried him there.
verses.50:13: And his sons carried him up into the land of Canaan and buried him in the double cave, which cave Abraham acquired as a possession for a tomb from Ephron the Hittite, opposite Mamre.
verses.50:14: And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers and those who had gone up with him to bury his father.
verses.50:15: Now when Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, "Perhaps Joseph will bear a grudge against us and will surely repay us for all the evils that we did to him."
verses.50:16: And they came to Joseph, saying, "Your father made us swear before he died, saying,
verses.50:17: 'Say this to Joseph, "Forgive them their wrongdoing and their sin, because they did evil things to you."' And now, accept the wrongdoing of the servants of the God of your father." And Joseph wept while they were speaking to him.
verses.50:18: And coming to him, they said, "Here we are, household servants."
verses.50:19: And Joseph said to them, "Do not be afraid, for I belong to God.
verses.50:20: You planned against me for evil, but God planned concerning me for good, so that it might happen as it is today, in order that many people might be sustained."
verses.50:21: And he said to them, "Do not be afraid; I will sustain you and your households." And he comforted them and spoke to their heart.
verses.50:22: And Joseph resided in Egypt, he and his brothers and all the household of his father; and Joseph lived one hundred and ten years.
verses.50:23: And Joseph saw Ephraim's children to the third generation; and the sons of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph's thighs.
verses.50:24: And Joseph spoke to his brothers, saying, "I am dying, but God will surely visit you and will bring you up out of this land into the land that God swore to our fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob."
verses.50:25: And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, "In the visitation with which God will visit you, you will also carry up my bones from here with you."
verses.50:26: And Joseph died, being one hundred and ten years old; and they buried him and placed him in the coffin in Egypt.

notes.1:1: The Greek has the singular τὸν οὐρανόν, so this reads "heaven" (singular) and not "the heavens." The verb ἐποίησεν means "made."
notes.1:2: ἀόρατος καὶ ἀκατασκεύαστος means "unseen (invisible) and unformed (not yet furnished)," which is the Greek's own interpretation of the Hebrew pair. πνεῦμα θεοῦ is rendered "the Spirit of God"; the phrase can also mean "a wind of God."
notes.1:6: στερέωμα means a firm or solid structure. "Vault" keeps that sense without the archaic "firmament" and is used for the word throughout.
notes.1:9: The second half of the verse (the water gathered and the dry land appearing) is a plus in the Greek and is translated as it stands.
notes.1:20: ψυχὴ ζῶσα (literally "living soul") is rendered "living creature" throughout Genesis 1–2, including 2:7, so the reader can see the same phrase recur.
notes.1:26: ἄνθρωπος is the generic word for a human being. It is rendered "man" to keep the singular collective, which the following "let them rule" picks up. The Greek has no "our" before "likeness."
notes.1:30: ψυχὴν ζωῆς is literally "a soul of life"; it is kept literal to show the Greek's distinct phrase.
notes.2:1: κόσμος here means "order, array, adornment" (the Greek word behind "cosmos" and "cosmetic"); it is rendered "adornment."
notes.2:2: The Greek reads "on the sixth day" God finished His works, so that the seventh day is free of work. The rendering follows the Greek.
notes.2:7: ψυχὴ ζῶσα is the same phrase rendered "living creature" for the animals in 1:20, 1:24 and 2:19. It is kept the same here so that the link stays visible. "Dust from the earth" stands in apposition to "the man" in the Greek.
notes.2:8: παράδεισος (a park or enclosed garden, from which "paradise" comes) is rendered "garden" throughout. The Greek spells the place Ἔδεμ (Edem); the standard English "Eden" is used.
notes.2:9: τὸ ξύλον τοῦ εἰδέναι γνωστὸν καλοῦ καὶ πονηροῦ is literally "the tree of knowing what is knowable of good and evil." In 2:17 the Greek uses the simpler phrase τοῦ γινώσκειν καλὸν καὶ πονηρόν.
notes.2:11: The Greek spells the names Φεισών (Pheison) and Εὑειλάτ (Heuilat); the standard English forms Pishon and Havilah are used.
notes.2:13: The Greek spells the river Γηών (Geon), rendered with the standard English form Gihon. The Greek has "Ethiopia" where the Hebrew has Cush; the rendering follows the Greek.
notes.2:16: βρώσει φάγῃ ("you shall eat with eating") echoes a Hebrew idiom. It is rendered "you shall eat for food," which keeps the dative noun.
notes.2:17: The Greek switches to the plural "you" (φάγεσθε) in this verse. θανάτῳ ἀποθανεῖσθε, "you shall die by death," is a Hebraic emphatic idiom kept literal; it means certain death.
notes.2:18: The Greek has the plural ποιήσωμεν, "let Us make," where the Hebrew has a singular. The rendering follows the Greek.
notes.2:23: The Greek pairs γυνή (woman) with ἀνήρ (man, husband). "Her man" keeps the wordplay; the same noun is rendered "husband" in 3:6 and 3:16.
notes.3:5: ὡς θεοί is plural, "like gods." The Greek does not make it a title for the one God here.
notes.3:8: ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ ξύλου is literally "in the midst of the tree"; the singular is taken as collective, "among the trees." τὸ δειλινόν means late afternoon toward evening.
notes.3:14: ἀπὸ πάντων is rendered "above all," meaning set apart in curse from all the other animals. "Earth you will eat" keeps γῆν; the Greek uses the same word as for the ground in 3:17–19.
notes.3:15: The Greek pronoun αὐτός ("he") is masculine, although its antecedent σπέρμα ("seed") is neuter. τηρέω means "watch, guard, keep watch for"; the Greek uses it in both clauses, so both get "watch for."
notes.3:16: Πληθύνων πληθυνῶ ("multiplying I will multiply") is an emphatic idiom, rendered "I will greatly multiply." ἀποστροφή means a turning or recourse; the Greek does not use a word for "desire."
notes.3:19: The Greek uses γῆ ("earth") in every clause, "you are earth, and into earth you will depart." It is kept so, not changed to "dust."
notes.3:20: The Greek translates the name as Ζωή, "Life." Following the Greek, the name is given as Life instead of Eve, which is the Hebrew-based name.
notes.3:23: παράδεισος τῆς τρυφῆς, "the garden of delight," is the Greek's rendering of the place name Eden.
notes.3:24: In the Greek, God "settled him opposite the garden," which is the Greek's own wording. The Greek uses the neuter article τὰ with χερουβίν, treating "cherubim" as a plural noun.
notes.4:7: The Septuagint reads "if you offer rightly, yet do not divide rightly, have you not sinned?" rather than the Masoretic Text's image of sin crouching at the door. The pronoun "his" (Greek autou) lacks an explicit noun for sin in the Greek and is often taken to refer to Abel, though "its" is also possible.
notes.4:16: Greek Naid is the Septuagint form of the region named Nod in the Hebrew text, and katenanti means "opposite" rather than "east of."
notes.4:18: The Septuagint reads the distinct names Gaidad, Maiel, and Methuselah (matching Methuselah in 5:21), corresponding to Irad, Mehujael, and Methushael in the Masoretic Text.
notes.4:22: The Septuagint has the shorter name Tubal rather than the compound Tubal-cain of the Masoretic Text.
notes.4:26: The Septuagint reads "He hoped to call upon the name of the Lord God," reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew verb than the Masoretic Text's "then people began to call."
notes.5:1: The Septuagint has the plural "human beings" (anthropon) rather than singular "Adam" in the opening title.
notes.5:3: Throughout Genesis 5, the Septuagint preserves a distinct chronology with higher pre-fatherhood ages for most patriarchs (such as 230 for Adam and 188 for Lamech) and corresponding differences in remaining years compared to the Masoretic Text.
notes.5:24: In 5:22 and 5:24, the Septuagint translates Enoch's walking with God as "pleased God" and renders "he was not, for God took him" as "was not found, because God transferred him," the wording echoed in Hebrews 11:5.
notes.5:29: The Septuagint reads "will give us rest" (dianapausei) rather than "will comfort us" (Masoretic Text), emphasizing the wordplay on the name Noah.
notes.6:2: The Septuagint reads "the angels of God" (hoi angeloi tou theou) here, whereas 6:4 reads "the sons of God" (hoi huioi tou theou), reflecting an early interpretive rendering of the Hebrew phrase.
notes.6:6: Greek enethymēthē ("took it to heart") and dienoēthē ("thought it over"), followed by ethymōthēn ("I have become angry") in 6:7, soften the Hebrew anthropomorphisms of divine regret and grief.
notes.6:14: Greek xylōn tetragōnōn ("squared timbers") and nossias ("nests," i.e., compartments) represent the Septuagint's rendering of the Hebrew terms for the ark's wood and rooms.
notes.6:16: Greek episynagōn ("tapering together") interprets the rare Hebrew term for the ark's roof or opening as narrowing the upper structure to a one-cubit finish.
notes.7:4: Greek anastema (also in 7:23) literally refers to that which stands upright or a living structure, serving as the Septuagint term for every living creature.
notes.7:11: The Septuagint dates the outbreak of the flood to the twenty-seventh day of the second month (matching 8:4), ten days later than the Masoretic Text's seventeenth day.
notes.7:17: The Greek text repeats "upon the earth" and includes "and forty nights" alongside "forty days," harmonizing with 7:4 and 7:12.
notes.8:2: The Greek source reads apekalyphthēsan ("were uncovered"), an early transcriptional variant attested in witnesses such as Codex Alexandrinus for epekalyphthēsan ("were covered over" or "closed").
notes.8:5: The Septuagint places the appearance of the mountaintops in the eleventh month rather than the tenth month as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.8:7: The Septuagint adds "to see whether the water had subsided" and states that the raven "did not return" until the water dried up from the earth.
notes.8:22: The Septuagint pairs "summer and spring" (theros kai ear) rather than "summer and winter."
notes.9:1: The Septuagint adds "and gain mastery over it" at the end of the blessing (echoing Gen 1:28), a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.9:6: The Septuagint reads "in return for his blood it will be shed" (where the Hebrew has "by man his blood shall be shed") and uses the first-person "I made" rather than the third-person "he made."
notes.9:21: The Septuagint reads "in his house" here (and "in the houses of Shem" in 9:27) where the Hebrew text reads "tent(s)."
notes.9:25: Greek "pais oiketes" ("a household servant") renders the Hebrew idiom "servant of servants."
notes.10:2: The Septuagint includes Elishah among the sons of Japheth here (in addition to listing him as a son of Javan in 10:4), whereas the Hebrew text lists seven sons in 10:2.
notes.10:4: Greek "Rhodioi" ("Rhodians") reflects the form "Rodanim" (compare 1 Chr 1:7) rather than "Dodanim" in the Hebrew text of Genesis 10:4.
notes.10:8: Greek "gigas" ("giant," also in 10:9) translates the Hebrew "gibbor" ("mighty one").
notes.10:12: Greek "Dasem" corresponds to "Resen" in the Hebrew text; similarly, Greek "Dasa" in 10:19 corresponds to Hebrew "Lasha."
notes.10:24: The Septuagint includes Cainan (Greek "Kainam") between Arphaxad and Shelah, as in Luke 3:36, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text omits him (note also that the Septuagint reads "Meshech" for Hebrew "Mash" in 10:23 and omits "Obal" in 10:28).
notes.11:1: Greek cheilos literally means "lip," preserving the Hebrew idiom for "language" (likewise in 11:6 and 11:9).
notes.11:4: The Greek reads "before being scattered" (pro tou diasparēnai), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "lest we be scattered."
notes.11:9: The Septuagint translates the name into Greek as Synchysis ("Confusion") rather than transliterating "Babel," and in 11:8 adds "and the tower."
notes.11:13: The Septuagint includes Cainan as a generation between Arphaxad and Shelah (cf. Luke 3:36) and gives longer ages before fatherhood across 11:12-25 than the Masoretic Text.
notes.11:28: The Greek reads "the country of the Chaldeans" (also in 11:31) rather than "Ur of the Chaldeans" as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.12:6: The Septuagint translates the location as "the tall oak" (ten dryn ten hypseilen) rather than transliterating "Moreh."
notes.12:8: "Toward the sea" (kata thalassan) is the biblical idiom for westward, toward the Mediterranean Sea (likewise in 13:14).
notes.12:9: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew geographical term Negev as "the wilderness" (also in 13:1 and 13:3).
notes.12:16: The Greek lists "mules" (hemionoi) where the Masoretic Text has "female donkeys," and in 12:20 adds "and Lot with him."
notes.13:4: This Greek text reads "where he had made the tent there" (ten skenen), a notable variant alongside manuscripts reading "at the first" (ten archen).
notes.13:5: The Septuagint reads "livestock" (ktene) where the Masoretic Text reads "tents."
notes.13:10: The Septuagint reads "God" here and in 13:13-14 where the Masoretic Text has the divine name YHWH.
notes.13:16: The Septuagint reads "the sand of the earth" where the Masoretic Text has "the dust of the earth," and in 13:17 adds "and to your seed forever."
notes.14:1: The Greek reads "in the reign" (Hebrew "in the days") and has distinct proper name forms here and in 14:2, 9: Thalga (Thalgal in 14:9; Hebrew Tidal), Balla (Hebrew Bera), Sennaar (spelled identically to Shinar in Greek; Hebrew Shinab), and Balak (Hebrew Bela).
notes.14:5: The Greek translates Hebrew Rephaim as "giants," renders Hebrew "Zuzim in Ham" as "strong nations with them," and reads "the Somaites in the city of Shaveh" (Hebrew "Emim in Shaveh-kiriathaim").
notes.14:11: Here and in 14:16, 21, the Greek reads "the cavalry" (τὴν ἵππον), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew term for "possessions" (rekhush) as "steeds" (rekhesh).
notes.14:13: "The migrant" renders Greek τῷ περάτῃ (literally "the one who crossed over"), the Septuagint's translation of Hebrew "the Hebrew"; Greek also has Aunan (Hebrew Aner) here and in 14:24, and Chobal (Hebrew Hobah) in 14:15.
notes.15:2: Where the Hebrew has an obscure phrase usually rendered "heir of my house," the Greek reads "the son of Masek my houseborn woman," treating the Hebrew word mesheq as a personal name.
notes.15:6: The Greek reads "God" and the passive "it was reckoned" (Hebrew has the divine name and active "he reckoned it"), the wording later quoted in Romans 4:3 and Galatians 3:6.
notes.15:11: The Greek reads "Abram sat down with them" (συνεκάθισεν), reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants vocalized as "drove away" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.15:15: The Greek reads "nourished" (τραφεὶς) where Hebrew has "buried," and in 15:17 reads "a flame" (φλὸξ) where Hebrew has "darkness"; in 15:19 the Greek spells "Kelmonites" (Hebrew Kadmonites) and includes the Hivites in 15:21.
notes.16:1: The Greek spells her name Sara (Σάρα) throughout Genesis 11–16 before lengthening it to Sarra (Σάρρα) in 17:15; standard modern English Sarai / Sarah is used consistently across chapters 11–17.
notes.16:12: "A wild man" translates Greek ἄγροικος ἄνθρωπος (literally "a rustic" or "untamed man"), corresponding to Hebrew "a wild donkey of a man."
notes.16:13: Both here and in the well's name in 16:14 (Φρέαρ οὗ ἐνώπιον εἶδον, corresponding to Hebrew Beer-lahai-roi), the Greek uses ἐνώπιον ("in person" or "face to face").
notes.17:1: The Greek reads "your God" (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "El Shaddai") and "be well-pleasing" (for Hebrew "walk").
notes.17:14: The Greek specifies "on the eighth day," a phrase also found in the Samaritan Pentateuch though absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.17:15: The Greek changes the name from Sara (Σάρα) to Sarra (Σάρρα), corresponding to the Hebrew shift from Sarai to Sarah; standard modern English Sarai / Sarah is used consistently.
notes.17:16: The Greek reads "a child" and shifts to masculine pronouns ("bless him," "he will become," "from him"), referring to the promised son rather than to Sarah as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.17:20: The Greek reads "twelve nations" (δώδεκα ἔθνη), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "twelve princes."
notes.18:7: The Greek source text reads the plural verb "they took" (ἔλαβον, as in Codex Alexandrinus) before returning to singular verbs for Abraham, whereas other witnesses read singular "he took" (ἔλαβεν).
notes.18:10: The Greek idiom "in due season" (εἰς ὥρας, also in 18:14) denotes the return of the same season in the following year.
notes.18:12: The Greek reads "It has not yet happened to me until now," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("Shall I have pleasure?").
notes.18:23: The Greek frames Abraham's opening appeal as a prohibition ("Do not destroy") and includes "and the righteous will be like the ungodly" here as well as in 18:25.
notes.18:30: "Let it be nothing, Lord" renders an elliptical Greek apologetic idiom (Μή τι, κύριε, also in 18:32) asking the Lord not to take offense.
notes.19:4: In the Greek text, "before lying down" concludes the preceding sentence ("and they ate before lying down"), whereas the Hebrew MT attaches it to the following clause ("Before they lay down, the men of the city...").
notes.19:5: The Greek uses the verb synginomai ("be with" / "have relations with"), a standard Greek euphemism for sexual intercourse, rather than translating the Hebrew idiom "know" literally.
notes.19:16: The Greek reads plural "they were troubled" (where the Hebrew MT has singular "he lingered") and plural "their hand" alongside the singular possessives "his wife" and "his two daughters."
notes.19:25: The Greek includes the clause "in which Lot was dwelling" (echoing 19:29), which is absent from the Hebrew MT.
notes.19:38: The Greek names the child "Amman" (with "the son of my kindred" as an explanatory appositive) and his descendants "Ammanites," corresponding to Hebrew "Ben-Ammi" and "Ammonites."
notes.20:2: The explanatory clause "for he was afraid to say, 'She is my wife,' for fear that the men of the city might kill him on account of her" is present in the Greek text and absent from the Hebrew MT.
notes.20:3: Greek ἐν ὕπνῳ means "in sleep" (Hebrew "in a dream"); likewise καθ᾽ ὕπνον in 20:6; 31:11, 24.
notes.20:14: The Greek adds "a thousand didrachmas" (anticipating 20:16) and uses the earlier form of the name "Abram" here, whereas the surrounding verses use "Abraham."
